newsitem.title: USA: Witness says McVeigh wanted to bomb Okla. building.
newsitem.headline: Witness says McVeigh wanted to bomb Okla. building.

text.p: Lori Fortier, a key witness in the government's case against accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh, testified in his trial Tuesday that he told her he wanted to blow up the Oklahoma City federal building.

Testifying with immunity from prosecution, Fortier said McVeigh was upset about the FBI's assault on the Branch Davidian compound in Waco, Texas, in 1993 and wrote a letter saying he "wanted to take action against the government."
A couple weeks later, during a visit to the Fortiers' trailer in Kingman, Ariz., she testified that McVeigh "told us what he meant by take action was to blow up a building, a federal building."
Later, she said, "Tim specified the building he was planning on bombing was the Oklahoma City building."
She also testified that McVeigh intended to rent a truck to carry the bomb and described how he planned to make the bomb with racing fuel and ammonium nitrate inside barrels in the truck.

Fortier's husband Michael, an Army friend of McVeigh's, also is expected to be a key witness for the prosecution. Michael Fortier has admitted in a plea agreement with the government that he knew about McVeigh's alleged plans and did nothing to stop him.
Prosecutors say McVeigh rented a Ryder truck to carry the bomb that blew up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people.
